thread:
maria: Quick question — hitting a weirdness with service-account impersonation + OIDC token exchange in the Node SDK. I call the impersonation endpoint to exchange a signed JWT for an id_token/oidc token, but the resulting token's aud claim is the token endpoint rather than the target audience I passed. Repro below. Anyone seen this?

maria: repro (super condensed):
```js
const client = new ImpersonationClient({sourceCreds});
await client.generateIdToken({target_audience: 'https://api.myapp/internal'});
// token.aud ends up as "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token" instead of our target_audience
```

john: Are you doing a signed JWT (JWT_ASSERTION) exchange or using the token endpoint's target_audience param? The aud claim in the signed JWT vs the resulting id_token can differ depending on the flow.

maria: I sign a JWT with sub=svc-account@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com and aud=https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, then POST to /token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer and include target_audience in body. The SDK's helper wraps this but I logged the raw request — target_audience is sent.

olivia: quick FYI — some token exchange implementations ignore target_audience for JWT grant_type and only honor it on the OIDC v1 token exchange flow. The Node helper has two modes: exchangeJwtForAccess (legacy) and exchangeForIdToken (OIDC). Make sure you're calling the OIDC path. Which method on the ImpersonationClient did you use? :thinking_face:

maria: I'm using generateIdToken which I expected to pick OIDC. Code is from our internal utils (`auth/impersonate.ts`).

sam: If you built the signed JWT manually, double-check the JWT claims. For OIDC exchanges some servers require the incoming JWT to have a specific audience (like the token-exchange endpoint URL) and then the server emits an id_token whose aud is what you requested — but other servers will override. As a workaround you can call the explicit id_token endpoint we have: POST /v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/:impersonate:generateIdToken (this is what the SDK should call).

kevin: Also note streaming clients: if you open a long-lived stream (we see this in the speech/stream client), the SDK caches the token and only refreshes at refreshThreshold. If the exchange mode returns a token with the wrong aud once, that cached token propagates. For quick test, set env REDWOOD_AUTH_REFRESH_MS=30000 to force faster refreshs.

john: Another debugging trick: inspect the id_token payload after exchange (`jwt.decode(id_token, {complete: true})`) to confirm which flow produced it. If aud==token endpoint, the server likely returned an access_token style token in an id_token slot.

maria: thanks — I decoded it and aud is the token endpoint. Looks like the SDK helper fell back to legacy exchange when source credentials were a JWT (service account key). If I switch to ADC (Application Default Credentials) with gcloud auth application-default login it hits the proper endpoint.

olivia: That matches my previous run. Fix: update impersonation helper to prefer the explicit generateIdToken RPC when target_audience is provided. I'll sketch a patch.

maria: sweet. If you want I can open the PR and include the minimal unit test (mock token endpoint) and a repro script. Will ping for reviews. :thumbsup:

kevin: please include a test for long-lived streams (simulate token caching + refresh) — we had a production outage where the fallback path produced wrong aud for 30 min. Ticket #INF-4523. infra-bot: linking INF-4523.

infra-bot: INF-4523 referenced: https://internal.redwood.ai/infra/INF-4523 — added owners @kevin @olivia

sam: small note for the PR: call out behavior for non-GCP identity providers (some of our on-prem flows expect different audience handling). A short doc blurb in the helper would save future head-scratching.

maria: will do. PR incoming in ~1h, I'll add the test and docs. Thanks everyone!
